text:
Cutter Gauthier's goal streak finally ended in Denver, where Scott Wedgewood and the Avalanche shut the Ducks out, and the headlines since have been about what he was chasing. Daily Faceoff has him next to Leon Draisaitl at the front of the Rocket Richard race. He has 16 points in his last 10 games against 11.5 expected, and Sportsnet's Eric Engels wondered whether his contract might end up looking cheap.

The rest of the week went the other way. Anaheim is winless in four (0-4-0), outscored 18-10, with only 45% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) in that run, so the slide is real. Then the bodies started falling: Beckett Sennecke landed on injured reserve, and Leo Carlsson left Saturday's loss in Utah with an upper-body injury and is listed day to day.

The goaltending hasn't helped. Lukas Dostal has an .833 save rate and is 8.6 goals worse than expected over his last five starts, and Ville Husso is at .825. As a team, the Ducks have allowed about 10.6 more goals than their chances against predict.

At 11-13-1 with 49% of the expected goals, the record is close to honest, and our playoff odds are down to 35%. Captain Mikael Granlund's top line with Gauthier and Sennecke has outscored teams 7-5 at 5-on-5 on just 43% of the chances. What we'd watch: who plays beside Gauthier while the injuries pile up, and whether either goalie strings together a week of saves.
headline: Gauthier's streak ends as the Ducks' slide deepens
